key_insight: Destructive testing indicates that SMAW produced mechanically sound low-carbon steel pipeline joints, although weld-metal impact toughness was lower than that of the base metal.
engineering_relevance: The findings support SMAW for low-carbon steel pipeline fabrication when joint strength, toughness, and bend performance are verified.
method: Evaluate weld metal, heat-affected zone, and base metal using hardness and Charpy impact tests.
Measure welded-joint tensile strength and resistance to cracking during bending.
Examine weld geometry and penetration macroscopically.
evidence_signal: Two welded samples achieved ultimate tensile strengths of 569.26 and 566.52 MPa; average Charpy energies were 132.9 J for weld metal, 237.1 J for the heat-affected zone, and 247.4 J for base metal, with no cracking or breaking reported in bend tests.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify Charpy test temperature or pipeline acceptance criteria, limiting conclusions about service suitability.
paper_title: Investigation of Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW)Weld Integrity on a Low- Carbon Steel Pipeline using Destructive Mechanical Testing Technique
